summary.text: Cliff Bentz is the Republican nominee for re-election to Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2021. A third-generation Oregonian raised on a family cattle ranch, he practiced water and ranch-reorganization law in Ontario for decades and served in both chambers of the Oregon Legislature before winning Congress in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Cliff Bentz is a third-generation Oregonian who was raised on his family's cattle ranches in Harney County; he attended Regis High School near Salem and graduated in 1970.
He graduated cum laude from Eastern Oregon State College with a bachelor's degree in history and business in 1974 and earned a J.D. from Lewis and Clark Law School in 1977.
Bentz joined the Yturri, O'Kief, Rose and Burnham law firm in Ontario in 1977 and became a partner four years later, specializing in ranch reorganizations and water law.

While practicing law, he served eight years as a member and then chair of the Oregon Water Resources Commission and as a director and chair of the Ontario 8C public school board; he also served on the Project Dove (domestic violence prevention) board, the Eastern Oregon University Foundation Board and the Oregon Historical Society Board.

Bentz was appointed to the Oregon House of Representatives (District 60) in January 2008, was elected that year, and served five two-year terms, including on the Revenue, Transportation, Energy and Environment and Joint Tax Credits committees.

He resigned from the Oregon House in 2018 when he was appointed to the Oregon Senate (District 30), where he served on the Finance and Revenue, Judiciary, Energy and Joint Tax Credits committees, and resigned January 2, 2020, to campaign full-time for Congress.
Bentz was elected to the U.S. House on November 3, 2020, and took office in 2021; he won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 79.6% of the vote.
In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on Natural Resources, with subcommittee assignments listed on Ballotpedia.
According to his official biography, he married Dr. Lindsay Norman, a veterinarian who practices small animal medicine in Ontario, in 1987.
